clue.text: Shortages damage large towns

parts.note: to damage something can mean to scar it
cities are large towns

explanation.surface: A complaint that wrecking big towns leaves people short of supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortages and scarcities are synonyms: both mean there is not enough of something.

clue.text: Hack crossing Portugal gets place on front page?

indicators.note: crossing means stretching across, so one piece goes over the other

parts.note: to hack is to slash
P is the international vehicle code for Portugal

explanation.surface: A journalist covering Portugal gets a story onto the front page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' suggests a journalist, but it means to cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a story prominent newspaper coverage is to splash it, a newspaper idiom.

clue.text: Come onto the scene in a contemporary broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means put on air, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a contemporary is a peer, someone of the same age

explanation.surface: A modern radio show where someone makes a debut.
explanation.definitionFit: To come into view or arrive is a synonym of turning up or emerging.

clue.text: Walk through the law

definitions.meaning: a stroll taken for health is called by this name
something permitted by the constitution is lawful in this sense

explanation.surface: A route that cuts through the legal system.
explanation.definitionFit: A health-giving walk is one sense; being in accord with the state's foundational law is the other.

clue.text: Sanctimonious bunch suppressed by international high-flier

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match
pi is a slang short form of pious, meaning sanctimonious
a lot is a group or bunch

explanation.surface: A holier-than-thou group kept down by a global high achiever.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is a cricket match between national teams.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot who tries out new aircraft literally flies high, a playful sense of the term for a star performer.

clue.text: Leak from former lover you heard? Desperate, showing no heart

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: heard means the word is said aloud rather than spelt

parts.note: the letter U is said the same as the word you

indicators.note: no heart means the middle letters are removed

parts.note: dire means desperate

explanation.surface: Seeping from an ex who is in a bad way.
explanation.definitionFit: To exude is to ooze or seep out, much as liquid leaks.

clue.text: Stone circle parking area east of Argyll

parts.note: a circle is shaped like the letter O
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

indicators.note: the eastern end of a written word is its final letter, so take the last letter of Argyll

explanation.surface: Directions to a stone circle with a car park in Argyll, a Scottish region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parking area' looks like one idea but gives two letters, P and A.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is a gemstone, so it is an example of a precious stone.

clue.text: Varied options must include one job

indicators.note: must include means one piece goes inside the other
varied means changed around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Advice that a range of choices should cover a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must include' puts I inside POSTION, the anagram of OPTIONS from 'Varied'.
explanation.definitionFit: A post or appointment at work is called a job, a synonym.

clue.text: Transparency of woman hugging loveless idiot

indicators.note: hugging means surrounding the other piece

parts.note: Lucy is a woman's name

indicators.note: love is zero, the letter O, which is removed

explanation.surface: A frank account of a woman embracing a fool she does not love.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarity of expression is transparency, a synonym.

clue.text: Fishing-boat's single mistake, foregoing Southern relish

indicators.note: foregoing means going before, so the mistake comes ahead of Southern

parts.note: a smack is a fishing boat
single means one
a slip is a mistake

explanation.surface: A fishing vessel's lone error, preceding a tasty southern sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relish' looks like a condiment but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To show eager anticipation of something is to relish it, an idiom.

clue.text: Flower girl finally out of bed and home

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word girl

parts.note: someone out of bed is up
being at home is being in

explanation.surface: A flower girl at a wedding has finally got up and gone home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower girl' reads as one phrase, but 'Flower' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The lupin is a garden plant with tall spikes of blooms, an example of a flower.

clue.text: Is Columbus in a state with no black R&B?

indicators.note: being in a state means being agitated or disordered, so the letters are jumbled
with no tells us to remove a letter from the fodder

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Asks whether Columbus, the Ohio city, sits in a state without any Black rhythm and blues.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the B from ISCOLUMBUS, then rearrange ISCOLUMUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhythm and blues and soul are closely related African-American popular genres, so the abbreviation stands for this style.

clue.text: Lead actor set to return for new business venture

parts.note: the lead actor in a show is its star

indicators.note: to return means the word for set is read backwards

parts.note: to set something down is to put it

explanation.surface: A film's lead is set to come back, as if it were news about a new business.
explanation.definitionFit: A new company, especially a small tech firm, is called a startup in business jargon.

clue.text: Left to cover start of cricket, energised

indicators.note: to cover means to wrap round, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: someone who left a room exited it

indicators.note: start of points to the first letter of cricket

explanation.surface: A broadcaster leaving to report the opening of a cricket match, feeling lively.
explanation.definitionFit: Being energised and being excited both describe a stirred-up, animated state.

clue.text: Physical outcome for which runners perhaps pay?

definitions.text: Physical outcome for which runners perhaps pay?

parts.words: Physical outcome for which runners perhaps pay?
parts.note: a fungal infection is the price that runners may pay physically, and it is named after them

explanation.walkthrough: The clue sounds like sports injury in general, but the condition is literally named after runners: a fungal infection of the feet caught in changing rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: This fungal skin infection is commonly picked up by sportspeople in damp changing rooms, a consequence of their activity.

clue.text: Accept fans going topless for such commercial putsches

parts.note: to accept is to take

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: lovers of something are fans

explanation.surface: Accepting fans going topless at a commercial coup.
explanation.definitionFit: Buyouts of firms are corporate seizures of control, like a coup or putsch.

clue.text: A card game needing small contracts

parts.note: bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A bridge game needing small contracts, a term of bridge bidding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracts' looks like a bridge bid but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To shorten a text is to contract it.

clue.text: Look up drink in Japan as memento

indicators.note: up in a down entry means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a peek is a look
sake is a Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: Looking for a drink in Japan as a souvenir.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake is a reminder of something, a synonym.

clue.text: The tar developed during cooking is overwhelming

indicators.note: during means one piece sits within the other

parts.note: baking is a kind of cooking

indicators.note: developed means worked into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Tar forming while food bakes is deeply unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' looks like photographic processing but signals the anagram; 'during' places it within the cooking word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stunning enough to make you gasp is overwhelming, a near-synonym.

clue.text: Refrain from mounting pictures in support of staff

indicators.note: in support of means being below, so the art piece comes under

parts.note: to staff is to man

indicators.note: mounting means climbing up, so in a down entry the word is read backwards

parts.note: pictures are art

explanation.surface: Holding back from hanging pictures supporting staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refrain' looks like a verb but means a repeated phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A refrain is a phrase repeated, like a chant.

clue.text: Reduce without a second order

indicators.note: without means some letters are taken away

parts.note: to decrease is to reduce

explanation.surface: Cutting back a second time without an order.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree is an official order.

clue.text: Almost suggest poem and go off

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite complete, losing its final letter

parts.note: to suggest something indirectly is to imply it
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: Hinting at verse before things go wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To go off can mean to blow up, and collapsing violently inwards is a kind of bursting.

clue.text: Old crowd rises to offer praise

parts.note: ex means former or old

indicators.note: rises means going up, so in a down entry the word is reversed

parts.note: a lot is a group, a crowd

explanation.surface: An elderly crowd stands up to applaud.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly.

clue.text: Tangoes wildly in front of the audience

indicators.note: wildly signals that the letters run out of order

explanation.surface: A dancer doing tangos with abandon in front of the spectators.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer in front of the audience is in view on the platform of a theatre, the idiom for being in performance.

clue.text: Protector ultimately failing a new supporter's pledge

indicators.note: the final letter fails to appear, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a guard protects
a golf tee supports the ball

explanation.surface: A bodyguard letting down a fresh backer's promise.
explanation.definitionFit: A guarantee is a formal promise, a synonym for pledge.

clue.text: Bury's at home — they're missing regulars

parts.note: at home means in

indicators.note: missing the regular letters means keeping only alternate ones of the word they're

explanation.surface: A football team from Bury, the Lancashire town, playing at home without its regular players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bury' looks like the town and club; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter a body is to bury it in the ground, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Discard from East, covered by spades, hearts and diamonds

indicators.note: covered by means the piece sits inside the others

parts.note: S is the card abbreviation for spades
H is the card abbreviation for hearts
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A bridge player sitting East throwing away a card while holding three suits.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the players are named by compass points, so 'East' fits the card-table picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed something is to get rid of it, so it is a synonym of discard.

clue.text: Shuts short road after hospital's lucky escape

indicators.note: after means the road piece follows the hospital piece

parts.note: shuts means closes
H is the road-sign abbreviation for hospital
Ave is the short form of avenue, a road

explanation.surface: A road closure near a hospital leading to a near miss.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow avoidance of disaster is idiomatically called this, from shaving too near the skin.
